description: The figure is a multi-level donut (sunburst) chart summarizing the task-wise class distribution for the TiALD dataset by first separating items into “Abusive” versus “Not Abusive,” and then further subdividing them by abuse type and sentiment/polarity. At the top level there are 2 slices: “Abusive” (teal) occupying a little over half of the circle (roughly ~55–60%) and “Not Abusive” (light yellow) making up the remainder (roughly ~40–45%). The next ring shows 5 labeled subcategories under “Abusive” (teal shades)—“Other” (largest), “Political” (second largest), “Racial” (small), “Sexist” (small), and “Religious” (very thin)—and 5 under “Not Abusive” (yellow shades)—“Other” (largest), “Political” (next), “Religious” (smaller), plus very small “Racial” and “Sexist” slices. The outer ring breaks each of these subcategories into sentiment slices labeled “Negative,” “Neutral,” “Mixed,” and “Positive” (where present): for abusive “Other,” the outer ring is almost entirely “Negative” with a small “Mixed” segment; for abusive “Political,” “Negative” dominates with a smaller “Mixed” portion; the abusive “Racial,” “Sexist,” and “Religious” portions appear essentially “Negative” only (each as a single negative-colored arc, with “Religious” extremely thin). For not abusive “Other,” the outer ring contains multiple sentiments with “Positive” and “Neutral” taking most of that arc and smaller “Negative” and “Mixed” slices; for not abusive “Political” and “Religious,” all four sentiments are shown as separate wedges with “Negative”/“Neutral” appearing larger than “Mixed”/“Positive” by visual area; and the tiny not abusive “Racial” and “Sexist” areas are split into very thin sentiment wedges. There is no separate legend and no numeric percentage annotations; labels are written directly on the slices, and no segments are exploded or otherwise visually emphasized, with slices arranged around the circle by the hierarchy rather than an obvious global descending-size order.
